text:
alex kim: Heads-up — I opened a docs PR to add Aegis2-13B to the model catalog. Focus: supported runtimes, sequence/response limits, benchmark numbers, and a short migration example for SDK v2. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/8123 :eyes:
maria ramos: nice! can you call out the CPU-quant fallback behavior? customers hit that on low-memory nodes last week.
alex kim: yes, added a 'CPU fallback' subsection. Short version: quantized CPU builds are supported but will incur ~3-4x latency vs GPU; we recommend fallback only for batch embedding workloads.
devon li: can we add a tiny benchmark table? like token/sec on small GPU (A100-40GB) vs CPU-quant (8x vCPU) so readers have ballpark numbers.
alex kim: good call. added numbers from the infra run: A100-40GB: 1200 tok/s, GPU-rtx6000: 820 tok/s, CPU-quant (8x vCPU): 320 tok/s. put them under "benchmarks (internal)" and marked as approximate.
maria ramos: snippet note: the SDK example currently uses SDK v1 methods — needs v2 migration. cc @devon li for the code tweak.
devon li: on it. propose replacing old call with:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(
    model='aegis2-13b',
    input='Summarize the infra report',
    max_tokens=256,
)
print(resp.text)
```
keep it minimal and streaming-safe.
alex kim: perfect. also fixed an internal link that pointed to the old runtime page — changed to https://docs.redwood.ai/inference/runtimes#cpu-quant-fallback
samir patel: small nit: sequence_limit is 8k default for Aegis2 but we allowed 12k with explicit config on Dedicated. Add that to the compatibility/limits section.
alex kim: added a short note: "Default sequence ceiling: 8k tokens (hosted). Dedicated customers can request 12k with appropriate runtime profile."
maria ramos: can we add a one-line migration tip for users moving from Aurora7B -> Aegis2? e.g., "reduce batch_size or enable KV-caching"
devon li: added: "If migrating from Aurora7B, lower batch_size by ~2x and enable prefix KV caching to avoid OOMs on smaller GPUs."
alex kim: CI is failing on one lint rule (md-link-check). I'm going to run linkchecker and update anchors. Command: `yarn doc-check && npx markdown-link-check docs/models/aegis2-13b.md`
docs-bot: Build started for PR #8123 — checks: markdown-lint, doc-build, link-check.
maria ramos: once CI green, can someone from infra confirm the A100 number? I used the run from `bench/aegis2/2026-03-15/` but want infra-approved tag. @samir patel
samir patel: I verified the A100 run id `run-20260315-aegis2` and numbers match within noise. Marked dataset reference in PR.
devon li: tiny docs language tweak: change "supported runtimes" to "supported deployment modes" for consistency with other model pages.
alex kim: updated wording. also added a brief fallback code snippet for CPU quant inference:
```bash
# start cpu-quant fallback container
docker run --rm -e MODEL=aegis2-13b redwood/cpu-quant:stable
  --max-seq 8192 --threads 8
```
maria ramos: LGTM. can you add an examples link under "See also" that points to `/examples/migration-aegis2`? users like hands-on guides.
alex kim: added an examples placeholder and filed a follow-up issue to populate with a notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/issues/229
docs-bot: All checks passed for PR #8123. Ready for review. :shipit:
maria ramos: Approved from docs side.
devon li: quick review done, one small wording nit in the intro (changed passive -> active).
samir patel: Approved from infra. add :white_check_mark:
alex kim: merging now. Thanks all!
maria ramos: great work — can we schedule a short blurb for release notes next week? I'll draft it. :tada:
